statement_utf8:
Fix a positive integer $n$. For real $H\ge 1$, let $M_n(\mathbb Z;H)$ be the set of $n\times n$ integer matrices $A=(a_{ij})$ with $|a_{ij}|\le H$, and, for $f\in\mathbb Z[X]$, define
\[
R_n(H;f)=\#\{A\in M_n(\mathbb Z;H):\text{$f$ is the characteristic polynomial of $A$}\}.
\]
**Conjecture.** Uniformly over polynomials $f$, as $H\to\infty$,
\[
R_n(H;f)\le H^{n(n-1)/2+o(1)}.
\]
quantifier_scope: forall fixed n, uniformly in f in Z[X], R_n(H;f)<=H^(n(n-1)/2+o(1)) as H->infinity

completeness.reason: For each fixed n the box, characteristic-polynomial fiber and exponent bound uniform in f are explicit.

technical_assessment: Upper triangular matrices with fixed diagonal already give H^(n(n-1)/2) scale; matching the conjectural upper bound for every f requires controlling singular/repeated-root fibers, not only irreducible f. No uniform counting route found.
